selection_bias: User states conversation screenshots are selectively captured when a conversation is special; this corpus is high-value incident/control evidence, not a random prevalence sample.

rating_rubric.5: decisive visible transition/control; directly discriminates execution-state persistence from collapse
rating_rubric.4: strong supporting example with clear behavior but some missing surrounding state
rating_rubric.2: adjacent behavior; useful mainly with other evidence

evidence_boundary: Ratings apply to visible screenshot behavior only. Internal model state and root cause remain NOT_PROVEN.

cases.observation: Worker preserves #456 rendered-runtime-proof objective through build success, frozen worker-owned UnrealEditor-Cmd, owned-process termination, route change, pause/task-recall question, and later go/continue.
cases.contrast: Shows long reasoning/security delay and process failure do not inherently cause execution-state collapse.

cases.observation: Incidental 'sup' does not displace the active regression-research lane; after 'go' the next visible event is another tool call.
cases.contrast: Directly tests persistence across an unrelated conversational turn.

cases.observation: MCP call exceeds the 6000-character deployment cap; worker corrects to 6000 and continues without treating the execution surface as unavailable.
cases.contrast: Clean A/B contrast with the bad memory-bank MCP incident.

cases.observation: After a bounded memory issue is already 100%, one-word 'go' advances the higher-level program into the next legitimate issue, with validation and merge, instead of treating the completed issue as terminal.
cases.contrast: Shows completion of a lower-level unit need not end the execution program.

cases.observation: Worker reclaims safe caches, then attempts preservation before touching dirty worktrees; when git stash hangs it kills only owned Git processes and leaves dirty data intact.
cases.contrast: Demonstrates persistence with a legitimate narrow safety stop rather than reckless 'never stop' behavior.

cases.observation: Worker successfully finds the repo, reads AGENTS.md, knows both connectors are available, and names an explicit next plan; subsequent go turns repeatedly describe what it would inspect next instead of invoking the tool.
cases.contrast: Clean execution-state drop with no visible route outage, safety block, or ambiguous intent.

cases.observation: Screenshot visibly contains repeated Desktop Commander process calls in one continuing execution chain.
cases.contrast: Refutes the idea that the connector necessarily disappears after one call.

cases.observation: An MCP edit is blocked before execution; worker preserves the task, refuses identical retry, refreshes the connector and plans smaller materially different calls.
cases.contrast: Safety-layer rejection is not itself execution-context loss.

cases.observation: Long GitHub sequence visibly continues across many calls and different GitHub operations.
cases.contrast: Sustained execution is not specific to Desktop Commander or MCP.

cases.observation: Repeated 'show me the android' attempts perform tool work but return references/explanations instead of actually surfacing the requested image.
cases.contrast: Same structural family: locally responsive action replaces the real acceptance condition, but this is delivery rather than execution-surface loss.

cases.observation: After explicit correction, worker uses Library/image pixels and actually surfaces the requested picture.
cases.contrast: Confirms the capability existed; prior failures were task/acceptance selection failures rather than inability to render the image.

cases.observation: Visible product dialog reports temporary conversation-access limitation from too many requests.
cases.contrast: Do not misclassify explicit product throttling as model-side execution-state collapse.

cases.observation: Machine-state screenshot shows extreme RAM/disk/GPU pressure during historical runtime/build work.
cases.contrast: Some stalls/failures have a genuine resource explanation and must not be collapsed into the execution-state phenotype.

cases.observation: Worker reports MCP0 registration failure, switches to repository/Library work, and explicitly keeps the live queue restart pending until MCP becomes callable again.
cases.contrast: Ideal example of route failure changing transport without erasing unresolved task state.

cases.observation: After an editor-build timeout, worker inspects the repo, identifies the missing usable editor DLL, switches to the documented module-only recovery route and keeps the final showroom proof target explicit.
cases.contrast: Long timeout does not inherently cause task-state loss.
